The first step's yield lets the pre-hold re-arm run; it parks on holdLoop and the clock re-bases past it. Replace 'end(): wait until performance.now() > lastTs, clear holdLoop, then call bare `__renderOnce()`' with: end() waits past lastTs (and, under ?particleClock=sim, past the film particle time), clears holdLoop, and calls bare `__renderOnce()` only when the realtime chain is dead (a step issued an explicit-ts render, or frameTime.tsMs changed since begin). scene3d/film/README.md:29 ('Realtime takes (server-driven moving subjects) run on requestAnimationFrame with the pipelined pilot instead.'): add that realtime takes are RECORDED on the film grid. Grid point n is the first drawn display frame at wall t ≥ n/fps, stamped n/fps. A display frame covering several points is encoded once per point (held, recorder.grab([t…])); display frames between points are skipped; undrawn or backpressured points carry over to the next drawn frame; points after the last frame come from one final frame at the end pose. Every take is therefore a constant-rate stream of ⌈wall·fps⌉ frames (the planned count at speed 1) that the CLI muxes with -r fps, and report.realtime holds the counters.

BLOCKING (regression from the math-1/contracts-8 fix, scene3d/film/drone/flight_model.js applyGimbalLimits): the new roll band is lim = max(rollLim, |rT| + 2°), symmetric about level, and it breaks across the ±180° roll seam. The failure needs a target horizon roll that crosses ±180° while the gimbal lags by more than the 2° slack. The camera is then left on the far side of the seam, and the band, which shrinks as |rT| falls, pushes it the opposite way to the target: a mirror image of the target's roll. The clamp increases follow error, which contradicts the fix's own contract ('the limit only bounds follow error', stated in the module header, the createDrone docblock and the F5 test name), and it rotates faster than the preset's maxRateDeg. Repro 1: fpv.fpv-flip (default axis 'roll') flown with createDrone('cinema'), reached in the plan through the documented pilot.flightPreset override. Pre-fix, the camera held at 45° and never exceeded 4.00°/frame, the 120°/s maxRate. Now it rolls to about +154°, then at t≈4.2 s unwinds 154° backwards, mirroring the target (camR = −nomR + 2°), at 6.17°/frame (185°/s). Follow error reaches 171°. On heavy it is 5.78°/frame against a 2.67°/frame limit; indoor also changes. Repro 2: drone.canyon-run with roll: 3.0 (legal, spec.roll ∈ [−π, π]) and maxBankDeg 60 on a winding ctx.path, flown 'heavy'. At t≈1.1–2.8 s the camera holds +143° while the target is at −141°: 75° of error, with the image banking against the turn. The same inputs on the auto-chosen cinema preset are fine (max error 2.5°). In my sweeps the problem appears only through the pilot.flightPreset override. This also contradicts the fix report's claim of 'zero change over every technique × gimbal preset': fpv.fpv-flip × cinema/heavy/indoor changed, outdoors and indoors. Probes: /tmp/claude-1000/verify-drone/{cmp_all,seam,seam2,flip_series}.mjs; pre-fix comparison copy: /tmp/claude-1000/verify-drone/pre. The remedy is not trivial; I tried two on scratch copies. (a) Skipping the clamp when it would increase |wrap(rT − r)| fixes canyon-run, but fpv-flip then snaps 67°/frame when the band re-engages. (b) Also capping the correction at maxRate·h still gives 8°/frame, because the cap stacks with the follow loop's own maxRate rotation. A correct fix must never move the camera away from the target across the seam, and must keep clamp plus follow within maxRate·h, for example by folding the correction into wF's budget along F. Suggested test: fpv.fpv-flip (roll) on cinema/heavy, and canyon-run roll 3.0 + maxBankDeg 60 on heavy, at 24/30/60 fps. Assert per-frame rotation ≤ max(maxRateDeg/fps, 1.5 × the nominal's per-frame rotation) and that follow error never grows while the target's roll crosses ±180°.

REGRESSION introduced by the static-fade fix (contracts-3 / seams-2 / gate-2): world_query.describeHit picks the static whose capsule surface is nearest to the hit point. With the default radii (tree 2.5 m, prop 1.0 m; film/index.js passes no staticDimsOf), that distance is 0 for every capsule containing the point, and ties go to the lower row index. As a result the fade key can name a neighbouring placement instead of the one the ray hit. Combined with the new ctx.fadedIds 'seenThrough' rule in sensors.subjectJob, the take then fades the wrong draw, and the sensors count the real, still-visible occluder as seen through. Reproduced with throwaway probes using the real world_query + sensors (/tmp/claude-1000/perc-probe/clump.mjs, clump_e2e.mjs, props_prod.mjs). (a) Two trees 1.9 m apart: before the fade, visibleFrac 0 / occluderKind tree / occluderIds ['placement:05050000:scenery:0'] (the WRONG tree; the blocker is :scenery:1). After fading the named id: visibleFrac 1, occluderKind null, occluderIds []. Every subject ray is still blocked by the other trunk. (b) Production wiring (no catalogs): a hit on a large static's rim 2 m from its origin, with a barrel 0.7 m away, returns the barrel's key. Effect in a take: a random nearby prop or tree vanishes, the real occluder stays, the pilot and the take report believe the subject is fully visible, and neither a fade nor a reroute happens. This is the original failure scenario (subject stays hidden, nothing done) plus a false perception reading. Suggested fix: in describeHit, give a fadeKey only when identification is unambiguous. Rank candidates by horizontal distance from the hit point to the placement origin/axis, require that distance ≤ the placement radius, and return fadeKey null (so the existing reroute fallback applies) when a second candidate is within a margin. Optionally, in sensors.subjectJob, treat a faded id as seenThrough only when the hit point lies within that placement's radius of its origin.

math-0 / contracts-0 are only partly fixed. The camera now follows a moving subject, but a flown carry rig surges at the start of the take in the case index.js usually produces. That case is a subject already walking at prepare time (velocity ≥ 0.3 m/s, so referenceTrack extrapolates it) that keeps walking through the pre-roll. Cause: during the pre-roll the reference is held at p=0. liveUpdate(settle) therefore stores S.v = S.F = d(live − ref(0))/dt, which is the subject's full speed. Once progress runs, the reference moves at that same speed, so the correct offset velocity is about 0. startPose/liveDerivs still reset the drone with nominal velocity plus S.v (double speed), and the follower overshoots. Measured by /tmp/claude-1000/subject-verify/live_probe.mjs (subject 3 m/s north, reference extrapolated at 3 m/s): drone.chase comes 1.65 m (20%) closer to the subject (ratio 0.80); drone.lead goes 1.69 m (21%) farther (ratio 1.21); both take about 3 s to settle. classic.tracking-follow dips 0.21 m. This breaks the fix's own claim of 'no lag at constant speed' and its L1 ±15% bound. The L1 tests miss it because they only use a static reference. When the subject stands still during the pre-roll, the error is 0.00. Fix: in liveUpdate's settle branch, subtract the reference's own velocity, i.e. S.v = S.F = dT/dt − (refSubjectFn(p+h) − refSubjectFn(p))/h. Then add an L1 case with an extrapolated ctx.subjectAt and a subject that walks during the pre-roll.

problems: tooling-3 regression in tools/film/plan/compile.mjs resolveEnd, {bars} branch. The new edit-0 rule is `pickup = bp < -1e-6 || inT <= 1e-9; base = pickup ? Math.ceil(bp - 1e-6) : bp`. When song.offsetSec lands even slightly AFTER a downbeat, Math.ceil jumps to the next bar, so the first {bars:n} shot becomes about n+1 bars and every contiguous {bars} cut after it is one bar late. The old rule cut on the intended downbeat. This is easy to hit: `song analyze` prints section starts with one decimal (analyze.mjs mmss(), e.g. '0:15.0'), and a director copies offsetSec from that. Probe /tmp/claude-1000/-home-wbterminal/6e329a46-30dc-40e7-9675-ce2d76948f37/scratchpad/bars/probe2.mjs: verse downbeat at 14.98 s, offsetSec 15.0, shots {bars:2},{bars:3},{bars:4}+start:{section:2}. OLD: v1 0→3.97 (bar 9), v2 →9.97 (bar 12), no warnings. NEW: v1 0→5.97 (bar 10, 3 bars instead of 2), and a new warning 'c1 starts 2 s before v2 ends; v2 is trimmed to 4 s'. Without the explicit section start, the whole chain is a bar late. Also, offsetSec 8.001 on a t0=0 grid makes {bars:4} = 10 s instead of 8 s (probe.mjs in the same dir). offsetSec at or before the downbeat (14.98, 14.95) is unaffected. Suggested fix: treat an edit-0 start that is only slightly past a downbeat as on it. For example, `const fl = Math.floor(bp + 1e-6); base = pickup && (bp - fl) * grid.barLen > grid.period / 2 ? Math.ceil(bp - 1e-6) : (pickup ? fl : bp)`, or the reviewer's alternative: snap to the nearest downbeat when the shot started within a beat of a bar line.
